# uptrace_forecast_monitor (Resource)

Manages an Uptrace forecast monitor: it alerts when the value is projected to leave a range within a horizon, such as a disk filling up.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# Alert three days before a filesystem is projected to be 96% full.
resource "uptrace_forecast_monitor" "example" {
  project_id = uptrace_project.example.id
  name       = "Filesystem fills up on {{ .Attrs.host_name }}"

  params = {
    metrics   = [{ name = "system_filesystem_usage", alias = "$fs" }]
    query     = "sum($fs{state=\"used\"}) / sum($fs) as util | group by host_name | group by device"
    column    = { name = "util", unit = "utilization" }
    max_value = 0.96
    horizon   = "3d"
  }
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `name` (String) Monitor name. It may hold template variables, such as {{ .Attrs.host_name }}.
- `params` (Attributes) What the monitor queries, the range the forecast must stay in, and how far ahead it looks. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--params))
- `project_id` (String) Project ID this monitor belongs to. Changing this forces recreation.

### Optional

- `channel_ids` (Set of String) Notification channel IDs, such as uptrace_telegram_channel.id. Omit to leave the links alone, as when channels name the monitor in their monitor_ids; set [] to detach every channel.
- `description` (String) Alert description sent with each notification. It may hold template variables.
- `repeat_interval` (Attributes) How often a firing alert notifies again. Omit for the server's default strategy. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--repeat_interval))
- `trend_agg_func` (String) How a series' points combine into the trend an alert shows. Omit for the server default.
- `trend_sensitivity` (String) How much a value must move before the alert trend reports it. Omit for the server default.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) Monitor ID.
- `status` (String) Runtime status: active, paused, firing, no_data, warming_up or disabled.

<a id="nestedatt--params"></a>
### Nested Schema for `params`

Required:

- `metrics` (Attributes List) Metrics the query refers to, each under an alias such as $requests. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--params--metrics))
- `query` (String) MQL expression that produces the monitored value, such as `avg($cpu) | group by host_name`.

Optional:

- `absent_points` (String) How a point with no data counts: zero, ignore, or alert (a missing point breaches). Omit for the server default.
- `column` (Attributes) The query result column the monitor evaluates, and its display unit. Omit to evaluate the first column. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--params--column))
- `horizon` (String) How far ahead the forecast looks. A duration string: ms, s, m, h, d (day) or w (week).
- `max_value` (Number) The monitor fires when the forecast rises above it.
- `min_breach_points` (Number) Breaching points the at_least window rule needs. Omit for the server default.
- `min_value` (Number) The monitor fires when the forecast drops below it.
- `num_eval_points` (Number) How many recent points each check evaluates. Omit for the server default.
- `resolution` (String) Width of one evaluated point. A duration string: ms, s, m, h, d (day) or w (week).
- `seasonality` (String) Whether the model learns daily and weekly cycles. Omit for the server default.
- `time_offset` (String) How far back the evaluated window ends, for data that arrives late. A duration string: ms, s, m, h, d (day) or w (week).
- `window_rule` (String) How the evaluated points decide a breach. Omit for the server default.

<a id="nestedatt--params--metrics"></a>
### Nested Schema for `params.metrics`

Required:

- `alias` (String) Alias the query uses: $ followed by an identifier.
- `name` (String) Metric name.


<a id="nestedatt--params--column"></a>
### Nested Schema for `params.column`

Required:

- `name` (String) Column name, as the query names it.

Optional:

- `unit` (String) Display unit, such as milliseconds, bytes or utilization.



<a id="nestedatt--repeat_interval"></a>
### Nested Schema for `repeat_interval`

Required:

- `strategy` (String) default, fixed (every interval), linear or exponential (from min up to max).

Optional:

- `interval` (String) Repeat interval of the fixed strategy. A duration string: ms, s, m, h, d (day) or w (week).
- `max` (String) Last interval of the linear and exponential strategies. A duration string: ms, s, m, h, d (day) or w (week).
- `min` (String) First interval of the linear and exponential strategies. A duration string: ms, s, m, h, d (day) or w (week).

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# Import a forecast monitor by "<project_id>:<monitor_id>".
terraform import uptrace_forecast_monitor.example 456:789
```
